competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency verb is to create a repeating pattern, yet every sampled item ends in 'Which sequence correctly creates it?' with four ready-made sequences to pick between. Recognising a correctly built pattern is a weaker act than building one, and no sampled item has the pupil assemble anything.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Numbers and geometric shape names both serve as pattern elements and unit lengths of two and three both occur, but the objects and images strands the wording names appear only as the words 'rectangle, triangle, square' printed as text, never as actual objects or pictures to arrange.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Checking a six-element sequence against a stated two- or three-element unit is well within Grade 1 reach, and the repeating unit is always named explicitly rather than left to be inferred.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The stem wording alternates between naming a unit and naming a repeating group, but that is surface rephrasing of one identical task; across all eight seeds there is a single response format and no constructive or pictorial alternative.

competency_alignment.rationale: The wrong sequences are near misses that differ in exactly one position, sometimes early and sometimes at the end, so discriminating them requires tracking the unit through the whole sequence - which is the skill at issue.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numeric elements stay within the range a Grade 1 pupil handles by Quarter 3, and the shape vocabulary is limited to three plane figures already available to them.
